issues.text: Unlisted and inaccurate claim about the course structure. In track.yaml, DIP (design.l1.solid-dip) is in module `solid`; the module right before this one is `layered`; dependency injection is the current module `dependency-injection`. "The last two modules" therefore points the reader at solid+layered, not DIP+DI.
issues.quote: That is the payoff of the last two modules. DIP made `OrderService` depend on interfaces, and dependency injection made the concrete objects come from outside.
issues.fix: Replace with: "That is the payoff of DIP and of this module. DIP made `OrderService` depend on interfaces, and dependency injection made the concrete objects come from outside."

issues.text: Unlisted and overstated claim about the previous lesson. design.l1.wiring-the-container did not swap the notifier; its Try it only asked the reader which file would change for a hypothetical SmsGatewayNotifier (answer: one line in ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs). The repo at stage-1 still registers LoggingNotifier.
issues.quote: the last lesson swapped the notifier for the whole API by changing one registration
issues.fix: Replace with: "the last lesson showed that swapping the notifier for the whole API means changing one registration" and add a claim citing DonHang.Infrastructure/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs @ stage-1 (`services.AddScoped<INotifier, LoggingNotifier>();`).

issues.text: Too strong. PlaceOrderAsync also reads `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` (OrderService.cs:15, PlacedAt) and constructs `Order`; it does not call only the abstractions' methods. Claim 1 is scoped correctly ("only calls ... on them"), the lesson sentence is not.
issues.quote: `OrderService` asks for two abstractions in its constructor and calls only their methods.
issues.fix: Replace with: "`OrderService` asks for two abstractions in its constructor, and every call it makes to the database or the notifier goes through them."

issues.text: Absolute wording: a private field is still reachable via reflection, and console output can be captured by a test (Console.SetOut). The point stands, but "no outside code can read it" is stronger than C# guarantees.

issues.fix: Replace with: "it sits in a private field of `OrderPlacedTightlyCoupled`, so ordinary calling code has no way to reach it".
